articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Metering Standards and Directives' (Digest No.075)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Metering Standards and Directives
IEE Colloquium on Metering Standards and Directives
abstract: The author looks at: (i) international working groups which are writing or revising electricity metering standards; (ii) how these groups and various other groups, both national and international, interrelate; and (iii) what standards exist and why they are important, particularly within the framework of the procurement directives.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Metering Standards and Directives
abstract: The author investigates British and International Standards activities in relation to electricity metering and associated EEC/UK regulative matters. Here, he concentrates on present and future standards activities related to communications for electricity metering and related purposes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Metering Standards and Directives
abstract: The British Standards Institution (BSI) is the body responsible for preparing British Standards. It provides the gateway for UK representation in European and International Standards Organizations. It is a nonprofit organization formed by subscribing members and committee members and incorporated by Royal Charter since 1929. Here, the author covers the work of BSI Committees which are concerned with electricity metering standards with particular emphasis on European standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Standards, directives and level metrology (electricity metering)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Metering Standards and Directives
abstract: Engineers entering a profession in the electricity metering industry or for that matter, engineers who have several years experience in this field, probably find the legislation concerning electricity meters confusing. Many would have no clear idea, if any, of the relationship between National legislation, EC directives and metering standards. Here, the author outlines how all electricity meters used for tariff purposes have to comply with National regulations or EC directives. Currently, there are several statutory instruments and directions for electricity meters made under primary legislation and other regulations made under the European Council directive. In addition, depending on the accuracy class and technology used, electricity meters have to comply with various British and international standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
